cards.text: Last time, Aaron's staff sprouted almonds overnight, and the Israelites cried out, “Anyone who comes near the tabernacle of the LORD will die.” (Numbers 17:8, 13) Now the LORD speaks to Aaron, Moses' brother and Israel's priest (Exodus 28:1). He starts heavy: Aaron, his sons and his father's house must bear the iniquity involving the sanctuary.

cards.question: Then God narrows it down. Who must bear the iniquity involving the priesthood?

answers.text: The leaders of all twelve tribes

cards.text: But Aaron isn't running this solo, friend. God tells him to bring his brothers from the tribe of Levi, his father's tribe.

cards.question: God says those Levites will ___ Aaron and ___ him and his sons before the Tent of the Testimony.

cards.text: The Levites take Aaron's duties and ALL the duties of the Tent. That's being the new hire who gets told, “Oh, and also everything else.” But there's one line they can NOT cross.

cards.question: What must the Levites not come near?

answers.text: The furnishings of the sanctuary and the altar
The poles and the outer curtains of the Tent
The courtyard gate in front of the Tent

cards.question: If the Levites cross that line, only the Levites will die.

cards.text: The Levites do all the work at the Tent of Meeting, and no outsider may come near Aaron. Aaron himself takes the duties of the sanctuary and the altar.

cards.question: Why does God put Aaron on the duties of the sanctuary and the altar?

answers.text: So wrath may not fall on the Israelites again
So the Levites can rest on the Sabbath
So the Tent can be packed up faster

cards.text: Then God says, “Behold, I Myself have selected your fellow Levites from the Israelites…” I'm leaning in, friend. This is either a compliment or a chore chart.

cards.question: God says He selected the Levites as a ___ to Aaron, dedicated to the LORD to serve at the Tent of Meeting.

cards.text: But everything concerning the altar and what's inside the veil? That's for Aaron and his sons only. That service is theirs.

cards.question: God tells Aaron that the work of the priesthood is a gift too.
What happens to any outsider who comes near the sanctuary?

answers.text: They must be put to death
They must bring a guilt offering
They must leave the camp for a week

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Aaron, “Behold, I have put you in charge of My offerings.” The sacred offerings of the Israelites go to Aaron and his sons as their portion.

cards.question: God gives Aaron and his sons this portion only for Aaron's lifetime.

cards.text: From the most holy offerings, the part reserved from the fire belongs to them: grain offerings, sin offerings and guilt offerings. In the drawer, my portion was dust, friend, and I didn't even get the GOOD dust.

cards.question: Who may eat the most holy offerings?

cards.text: Then come the offering of their gifts and all the wave offerings of the Israelites. These belong to Aaron's family too, as a permanent statute.

cards.question: Every ceremonially clean person in Aaron's household may eat the gifts and wave offerings.

cards.text: The list rolls on: the freshest olive oil, the finest new wine and grain the Israelites bring as firstfruits, and every devoted thing in Israel all go to Aaron. That's more boxes showing up at one door than my bakery packs on its busiest day.
The firstborn of every womb offered to the LORD, man or beast, belongs to Aaron too. But some of those firstborn have to be bought back.

cards.question: Every firstborn son, and every firstborn male of ___ animals, must be redeemed.
What is the redemption price for a month-old boy?
Aaron may also redeem the firstborn of an ox, a sheep or a goat.

cards.text: Those three are holy, so their blood goes on the altar, their fat is burned as a pleasing aroma to the LORD, and their meat goes to Aaron. A pleasing aroma? Friend, I KNOW that one. I've opened an oven door and had three bakers fall in love at once.

cards.question: God seals all these holy offerings with a permanent covenant of salt before the LORD. Who is it for?

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Aaron, “You will have no inheritance in their land, nor will you have any portion among them.” No land, friend. Even in the junk drawer I had a little spot behind the takeout menus.

cards.question: If Aaron gets no land, what does God say is his portion and inheritance?

answers.text: The best fields by the Jordan

cards.text: Then God turns to the Levites, the ones doing the service of the Tent of Meeting. He's got something for them in return for all that work.

cards.question: God gives the Levites all the ___ in Israel as an inheritance.

cards.text: No longer may the Israelites come near the Tent of Meeting, or they will incur guilt and die. The Levites do the work, bear their iniquity, and receive no inheritance among the Israelites.

cards.question: God says the Levites get no inheritance among the Israelites because He gave them the tithe as their inheritance.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses to speak to the Levites, and here's the twist: the folks who RECEIVE the tithe have to give from it too. That's like your paycheck clearing and your first move is writing a check.

cards.question: How much of the tithe do the Levites present as an offering to the LORD?

cards.text: God says their offering will be reckoned to them as grain from the threshing floor or juice from the winepress.

cards.question: Who receives the LORD's offering from the Levites' tithes?
The Levites present the offering due the LORD from all the ___ of every gift.

cards.text: God says it again: once they've presented the best part, it's reckoned to them as the produce of the threshing floor or winepress. That line again, friend. When God says something twice, I write it on my apron.

cards.question: The Levites and their households may eat the rest of the tithe anywhere, as payment for their work at the Tent of Meeting.

cards.text: Once they've presented the best part, they won't incur guilt because of it. But God ends with a warning about the sacred offerings of the Israelites.

cards.question: What happens if the Levites defile the sacred offerings of the Israelites?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 5 quotes "Oh, and also everything else.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Moses appears here for the first time, in 'Moses' brother', but he is never introduced. He shows up again as an actor in stop 3 card 7 and is still never introduced.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Card 1 quotes the Israelites saying 'Anyone who comes near the tabernacle of the LORD will die,' and card 8 says 'no outsider may come near Aaron.' Together these hand the baker the answer to card 14 (an outsider who comes near the sanctuary must be put to death).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'The Levites take Aaron's duties' (and card 8's 'Aaron himself takes') changes the text's 'attend to your duties.' It reads as if the Levites take over Aaron's role, which echoes the 'replace' option the baker just ruled out on card 4.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The two right words, 'join' and 'assist', both fit either blank. 'Will assist Aaron and join him' reads just as naturally, so a baker who picks the right words in the wrong order could be marked as missing it.
findings.question: On a two-blank card, may the two right answers be swappable between blanks? Or must each right word fit only its own blank?

findings.problem: Numbers 18:8-19 is a list of which offerings go to Aaron's family, and it gets a whole stop with 7 choice cards, including memorizing details like the five-shekel price. prep-walkthrough.md lists 'rules for offerings and feasts' as a long stretch, which gets one summary card and no choice cards. But the whole chapter is God's speech to Aaron about these portions, and the doc also says 'speeches, teaching and key laws' are not long stretches.
findings.question: When a whole passage is a divine speech made of offering rules, is verses 8-19 a long stretch (one summary card, no choice cards, no stop of its own)? Or is it the heart of the passage and fair to ask about?

findings.problem: The joke blends the Bible setting into the comparison: the offerings become 'boxes showing up at one door.' The action also doesn't match. Aaron is receiving gifts, but the comparison is about his bakery packing boxes to send out.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: Card 1 says Aaron has no inheritance in the land, and the question itself opens with 'If Aaron gets no land.' That rules out both wrong answers, which are land: 'The best fields by the Jordan' and 'The city of Hebron.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Then God turns to the Levites' suggests God starts speaking to the Levites. In the text, the LORD is still speaking to Aaron about the Levites (18:20-24). God only sends a message to the Levites, through Moses, in 18:25-26.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
